concerns.message: One socket per sector gives the island away. The design says three sockets in three different sectors 'narrows the hunt without giving away the exact islet' (decisions.md, task Design). That can't be true. The map is public static content (§16; the client ships `sliceSeaSource`) and the socket positions are validated as distinct sectors, so sector maps one-to-one to socket. With 3 sockets and a sector-sized reveal, every layout leaves some socket alone in its sector. The only exception is all three in one sector, where the reveal tells nothing. So three sockets can never mean 'narrows but doesn't reveal'.
concerns.consequence: When `objectives-endgame` announces the sector at the first full set, every player knows the exact final islet. The full-set holder's exclusive 'exact route' (§5) is worthless, and the §3/§16 goal of keeping the final-island choice hidden fails by construction. The 'three different sectors' validator and the socket placement would both have to be redone later.

concerns.message: Adding the socket docks as ordinary Dock tiles puts them in `map.docks`: `createSeaMap` collects every Dock tile in row-major order. `packages/simulation/src/simulation.test.ts` ('moors every approach … at every dock', l.686–836) sails every dock and fails on any resting tile within 2 tiles of a berth that `allowedRests` doesn't list. That list is keyed by dock label. `dockRadius` is 384 (1.5 tiles), and each regular dock has two such tiles on the coast 2 tiles away. A ≤6×6 islet with a flat coast beside its dock will produce new ones, labelled '?, north dock (x,y)' because the dock's island is −1. Row-major insertion also shifts dock ids and changes which dock comes first in several places: `docks[0]` (web.test.ts:120/216, simulation.test.ts:632) and `docks.find(side === 'S')` (integration match.test.ts:135–168). And `seaModeRules` (encounters/modes.ts:55) would start respawning losers at socket docks.
concerns.consequence: `npm run test:unit` fails in a file the world lane doesn't own, which triggers the Stop rule ('a check can pass only by changing a path outside the owned paths'), so the lane reports blocked. If the geometry happens to dodge the resting tiles, dock ids and respawn points still change under encounters-online's respawn and docking tests, which is a merge conflict and a gameplay change the task rules out. Decide before starting: either keep socket berths out of `map.docks` (the socket carries its own claim tile), or approve an `allowedRests` edit coordinated with encounters-online and append socket docks after the regular 16.

concerns.message: The sketch mirrors into all four quarters. An islet in the quarter produces 4 copies, and one on a midline produces 2, so 'three sockets, may be placed symmetrically' can't happen. Three sockets need a new asymmetric overlay step in `sliceSeaTmj` after mirroring. Three asymmetric sockets also make some spawn slots systematically closer to the final island, and only the ≤90 s ceiling is checked.
concerns.consequence: The worker writes and tests a new overlay path in the sketch generator. Spawn fairness (§2) gets worse, and the travel validator doesn't measure it.

concerns.message: The existing `validateSeaMap` rejects islets that aren't islands. Socket land raises 'lies in 0 island rectangles'. A socket dock raises 'outside every island rectangle'. The travel section crashes on `islands[dock.island]!.name` for island −1. And a route from a socket dock to a same-quadrant regular dock fails the 'routes cross the hub' rule. Sockets have to be passed through the land, dock, nearest-island and hub checks, without disturbing the single-issue `toEqual([...])` assertions in the existing negative tests.
concerns.consequence: `map:build` refuses the map, or the hub or nearest-island checks fail, until those exclusions are written. This is rework inside owned paths if nobody plans for it.

concerns.message: The keep-clear rule (8 tiles from the hub, spawns, docks and the open row) doesn't cover the browser sail-and-dock route. `tests/e2e/sea.spec.ts` starts 14 rows south of Palm Key's south dock at (23,41). Its waypoints run around the shoal to x≈29, and its fog check uses open-sea tiles within sight of those waypoints. All of this is in sector (0,1), a natural place for a west socket. The rule also doesn't say whether the open row means all of row 58 or ±20 tiles of the hub, or which distance metric to use.
concerns.consequence: A placement that passes the new validator can break the browser suite, which the operator only runs at merge, so the islet would be moved late.

concerns.message: 'The grid is computed from the map size, as the intel module does', but no intel module or sector code exists at the base commit (no `sector` anywhere under packages). intel-core-fixes-2 is writing it in parallel. Nobody has decided which tile defines a socket's sector (its footprint, its dock, or its claim circle), and islets near the 37/74 boundaries could straddle two sectors.
concerns.consequence: The world lane's sector grid and intel's grid, or the announced sector of a straddling islet, may disagree. Then the 'different sectors' guarantee, or its replacement, doesn't hold for the reveal players actually see. Export one `sectorOf` from seaMap.ts, and require the footprint and the claim circle to sit inside one sector with a margin.

concerns.message: `hashState` and FNV-1a live in `packages/simulation/src/hash.ts`. `packages/content` can't import them, because simulation depends on content, not the other way round. The new socket field must also be optional on `SeaMapSource`: unowned tests build `SeaMapSource` literals without it (simulation.test.ts:96, encounters/*.test.ts).
concerns.consequence: Following the 'for example hashState' hint creates a circular import. A required field breaks `npm run typecheck` in files the lane doesn't own. Use a documented integer avalanche (Math.imul fmix32) inside content, and make the field optional.

concerns.message: Each extra dock in `map.docks` adds thousands of lanes to the 30 s docking test and one more start to the random-helm test (which shares one RNG stream across starts).
concerns.consequence: The docking test's run time goes up by roughly a fifth on a shared machine and could hit its 30 s timeout intermittently.

structured_output.simpler_alternative: Draw one ≤6×6 islet in the sketched quarter inside sector column 1, for example x≈40–46, y≈9–15. That keeps it clear of the 8-tile zones around spawn (31,5), the docks (17,21)/(23,27), the hub and row 58. The existing mirror then produces 4 sockets: two in the north-centre sector on either side of the x=55 shoal wall, and two in the south-centre sector. No overlay code is needed, all 8 spawns get equal treatment by symmetry, and a sector reveal still leaves two candidates, so it narrows the choice without giving it away. Replace the 'three different sectors' validator with 'every sector holding a socket holds at least two'. Store sockets as `finalSockets?: { rect, claimTile }[]` on SeaMapSource and SeaMapDefinition, and keep their berth tiles out of `map.docks`. Sailing, respawn, dock ids and the unowned docking tests stay untouched, which also matches 'changes no gameplay yet'. `chooseFinalSocket(map, secret)` then reduces a Math.imul avalanche of the secret modulo 4.
structured_output.cheap_experiment: About 15 minutes, on a scratch branch. Add one 5×5 islet with a single south-facing D tile to the sketch at x 40–44, y 9–13, then run `npm run map:build -- --from-sketch`. Then run `npx vitest run --project unit packages/simulation/src/simulation.test.ts -t 'moors every approach'`, plus `npx vitest run --project unit packages/content/src/maps.test.ts`. If the docking test reports '?, … dock (x, y)' resting tiles it doesn't list, or dock ids shift, socket berths have to stay out of `map.docks` (or the operator has to approve the unowned edit) before any worker starts. The `validateSeaMap` output from the same run lists every existing check that has to learn about sockets.
